firstMessage:
`Sessions.login` in `src/accounts.ts` now computes the password hash before it checks the lock, so a locked account takes as long to refuse a login as a wrong password does. The full suite passes (36/36), and the change is not committed.

The change is in `login`: the `hashPassword` call moved above the `now < c.lockedUntil` check and its result is stored in `attempt`, which the constant-time comparison then uses. A short comment explains why the order matters. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: a correct password is still refused while locked (R-LOGIN-LOCKOUT).

I did not add a test for the timing. Measuring it reliably would be flaky, and the existing lockout test still covers the behaviour.

Unknown emails still return before any hashing, so a login for a non-existent account is faster than either a wrong password or a locked account. That is a separate enumeration gap, which I left alone because you asked only about the locked case.
finalMessage:
I also closed the unknown-email gap I flagged last time. `login` in `src/accounts.ts` now runs a scrypt hash against a dummy salt when the email has no account, so an unknown email takes as long to refuse as a wrong password. The full suite passes (36/36). The change is not committed.

The dummy salt is a module-level random value, so the hash runs without revealing whether an account exists. The lock-check reorder from before is still in place.
